texto:
Amazon's public account of how many people watch The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power has changed in both size and measure since filming on the third season began. On June 12, 2025, Prime Video said the series had "attracted over 170 million viewers worldwide" and that season two was "the most-watched returning season by hours watched." At Amazon's Upfront presentation on May 11, 2026, the figure had become "over 185 million," and season two was "among the Top 5 most-watched returning seasons ever," ranked by viewers over a 91-day window. Neither number comes with a method. Season three premieres on Prime Video on November 11, 2026.
In Short
Amazon keeps telling people how popular its Lord of the Rings series is, but the numbers, and the way it counts them, have shifted from one press release to the next. In June 2025 Amazon said season two was the most-watched returning season by hours watched; by May 2026, at an event for advertisers, it said season two was in the top five, counted by viewers instead. That matters to the brands that buy ads on Prime Video, because the show returns on November 11 and Amazon has not explained who counts as a viewer or why the measure changed.
Two claims, eleven months apart
The earliest of the releases is dated June 12, 2025, under a Culver City, California dateline. It announced three cast additions for season three and gave the audience figure then in use: the series "has attracted over 170 million viewers worldwide" and "continues to be one of Amazon's strongest drivers for new Prime membership sign-ups," according to Prime Video. It ranked both seasons in a single sentence. "Season One remains the biggest TV premiere in the history of Prime Video, and Season Two is the most-watched returning season by hours watched." The show itself was "an unprecedented success."
By May 11, 2026, the wording had changed. In the release Prime Video issued during Amazon's annual Upfront presentation in New York, the series "has attracted over 185 million viewers worldwide." The rankings carried a new qualifier: "Through their respective 91 day post premiere launch windows and ranked by viewers, Season One remains the biggest TV series premiere in the history of Prime Video, and Season Two is among the Top 5 most-watched returning seasons ever." A third-party reference appeared for the first time, too. Season two "debuted as the #1 Original Series on Nielsen's Streaming Top 10 Chart and remained in the top 4 throughout its entire run," according to Amazon. "An unprecedented success" gave way to "one of the highest performing and most-viewed titles ever on Prime Video." Prime Video's July 24 release from San Diego Comic-Con repeated the May paragraph almost word for word.
Three things moved. The audience figure rose by 15 million, or about 8.8% - a PPC Land calculation - across eleven months in which no new episodes were released; season two arrived in August 2024, almost two years before the Upfront. The measure behind the season two ranking switched from hours watched to viewers. And the ranking itself went from first to somewhere in the top five.
Can the two statements be compared? Not directly. Hours watched reward depth of viewing; a count of viewers rewards reach. A season that leads on hours can sit lower when ranked by people, or the other way round, and the June 2025 statement named no time window at all. Amazon does not say whether season two still leads by hours, which returning seasons now sit above it by viewers, or how a viewer is defined - a person, a household or an account. Its own weekly Prime Video chart ranks titles by accounts and publishes no viewer totals.
The most recent release, dated October 21, 2026, carries none of these figures. The trailer announcement drops the viewer count, the rankings and the line about Prime sign-ups from its text, though the series press page still claimed 185 million viewers when the trailer went out.
The Upfront pitch
The Upfront is the event at which Amazon presents its programming to advertisers ahead of the year's advance-selling season, and the May 11 release was one of the Prime Video announcements made there. It confirmed the November 11 premiere and quoted Peter Friedlander, head of global television at Amazon MGM Studios.
"From the very beginning, this series has embodied the scale, ambition, and cinematic storytelling that define Prime Video's biggest global series," Friedlander said. "The extraordinary response from millions of fans around the world has made it clear that this journey through Middle-earth continues to resonate, and that momentum has only grown heading into Season Three."
The release does not put a number on that momentum. It described season three as "jumping forward several years from the events of Season Two" and set "at the height of the War of the Elves and Sauron, as the Dark Lord seeks to craft the One Ring that will give him the edge he needs to win the war." Later releases fixed the gap at five years since the fall of Eregion. PPC Land covered the full Prime Video Upfront slate on May 17.
For an announcement made at an advertising event, the release says nothing about advertising on the series. There is no sponsor, no ad format and no ad load. The only commercial language sits in the standard "About Prime Video" paragraph at the bottom.
Comic-Con: a shared slot in Hall H
Prime Video announced its 2026 San Diego Comic-Con program in a release headed July 9, 2026. The dateline in its body reads "July 9, 2025," but the panels it lists ran in July 2026. The Rings of Power did not get a panel to itself. It shared a 90-minute Hall H session on Friday, July 24, from 10:00 to 11:30 a.m., with the upcoming series Blade Runner 2099, billed as "Prime Video Presents Blade Runner 2099 and The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power." The rest of Prime Video's Comic-Con program covered Batman: Caped Crusader season two on Thursday, July 23, and Reacher with its spin-off Neagley, followed by Mike Flanagan's Carrie, on Saturday, July 25.
Over 6,500 fans were in Hall H for the Rings of Power segment, according to Prime Video's July 24 release. Showrunners J.D. Payne and Patrick McKay appeared with cast members Cynthia Addai-Robinson, Owain Arthur, Ismael Cruz Córdova, Charlie Vickers, Daniel Weyman and season three newcomer Jamie Campbell Bower. Benjamin Walker, who plays High King Gil-galad, moderated.
The panel debuted a teaser trailer and gave characters to actors whose casting was already public. Eddie Marsan plays "King Durin IV's older brother, 'Thrain'"; Andrew Richardson plays "Elendil's younger son and Isildur's brother, 'Anárion'"; and Adam Young plays "'Marnûkh,' a mysterious Orc who may not be what he seems," according to the release. Two more roles had been disclosed earlier that week: Bower as Celeborn, "Galadriel's long-lost husband," and Zubin Varla as "Khamûl the Easterling," of Rhûn.
One reveal concerned a creature rather than an actor. A featurette titled "Bringing Season Three's Creatures to Life," shown only in the room, previewed Fell-beasts, the war elephants known as Mûmakil, Orcs and the Balrog, which "for the first time ever will speak," according to Prime Video. The voice is Simon Pegg's. Midway through the panel, four figures in full armor appeared as Nazgnagôl, which the release describes as "ring-servants of Sauron" and "the earlier Second Age incarnation of the Nazgûl, also known as Ringwraiths, of the Third Age."
Seventeen months from cameras to premiere
The June 2025 release fixes the start of production. Season three "recently began filming at the series' new production home at Shepperton Studios in the UK," according to Prime Video. That release named Richardson, Varla and Young, with Richardson as a series regular and Varla and Young in recurring roles, but not their characters. Those were held back for more than a year, until the week of Comic-Con. From the June 2025 announcement to the November 11 premiere is about 17 months, a PPC Land calculation.
The production credits are consistent across the releases. Payne and McKay are showrunners and executive producers, joined by executive producers Lindsey Weber, Justin Doble, Kate Hazell and executive producer-director Charlotte Brändström. Matthew Penry-Davey is producer. Amazon's credits page lists Brändström, Sanaa Hamri and Stefan Schwartz as directors, and describes the series as "Based on The Lord of the Rings and Appendices by J.R.R. Tolkien." The season three press page carries 31 bios.
The release pattern is set. As PPC Land reported on October 21, the first four episodes arrive on November 11, episodes 305 and 306 on November 18, and the final two on November 25. All three dates are Wednesdays. The first two seasons, sixteen episodes in all, are available "exclusively on Prime Video in more than 240 countries and territories," according to Amazon.
The commercial paragraph
Across five releases spanning 16 months, the Rings of Power announcements never mention advertising on the series. What changed is the boilerplate around them.
In June 2025 the "About Prime Video" paragraph offered "more than 500 free ad-supported (FAST) Channels," add-on subscriptions from partners such as Apple TV+, Max, Crunchyroll and MGM+, and benefit sharing through "Amazon Household." By the May 2026 Upfront release, the channel count was "more than 900," the sharing scheme had been renamed "Amazon Family," the sports list had grown to include the NBA, NASCAR and The Masters Tournament, and US viewers could "watch and shop their favorite titles with the fan-fueled shopping experience Shop the Show." The July and October releases use a shorter text: "100+ add-on streaming subscriptions," "900+ FAST Channels," "Prime-exclusive tier 1 live sports," and one new sentence. "In April 2026, Amazon shared Prime Video is a large and profitable business in its own right."
Amazon's channel counts are not consistent between titles, either. PPC Land found "more than 800" FAST channels in a May boilerplate for The Terminal List, against "more than 900" in the Rings of Power Upfront release.
No figure supports the profitability sentence in any of the releases. Andy Jassy's April 9, 2026 shareholder letter, as PPC Land reported it, grouped Prime Video with Pharmacy and Grocery as newer businesses "improving their economics," without a Prime Video profit number.
The sign-up line is the one with the clearest commercial weight. Amazon repeated in June 2025, May 2026 and July 2026 that the series is "one of Amazon's strongest drivers for new Prime membership sign-ups." No count, attribution method or comparison set accompanies it. Why does it matter to advertisers? Because a new Prime member in the US sees ads by default. Amazon introduced ads to Prime Video in January 2024 and defaulted all subscribers to the ad-supported tier, and on April 10, 2026 the US ad-free option became Prime Video Ultra at $4.99 a month, up from $2.99. Members who do not pay for Ultra will watch season three on the AVOD version of the service. In its fourth-quarter 2025 results, Amazon put the average ad-supported audience at 315 million viewers globally.
The season arrives as Amazon's advertising growth slows. Third-quarter advertising revenue rose 11% to $19.64 billion, after 26% growth to $19.8 billion in the second quarter. Thursday Night Football, which shares the November schedule with the series, averaged 17.7 million viewers through six games, according to Nielsen as cited by Amazon. Amazon does not report Prime Video advertising revenue on its own, and none of the Rings of Power releases says whether season three has a launch sponsor, a set ad load or packaged inventory for a three-week run that ends two days before Black Friday.
What Amazon has not said
- How a viewer is counted in the 170 million and 185 million figures, and over what period.
- Why the season two ranking moved from hours watched to viewers, and whether the series still leads on hours.
- Which returning seasons rank above season two by viewers.
- How many Prime sign-ups the series has produced, or how they were attributed.
- Whether any advertising arrangement exists for season three.
Timeline
- September 2, 2022 - The Rings of Power season one debuts on Prime Video
- January 2024 - Amazon introduces ads to Prime Video and defaults subscribers to the ad-supported tier
- August 2024 - Season two arrives
- June 12, 2025 - Prime Video adds Andrew Richardson, Zubin Varla and Adam Young to the cast; filming has begun at Shepperton Studios; Amazon cites over 170 million viewers and calls season two the most-watched returning season by hours watched
- February 2026 - Amazon reports an average ad-supported Prime Video audience of 315 million for Q4 2025
- April 9, 2026 - Jassy's shareholder letter groups Prime Video among newer businesses "improving their economics"
- April 10, 2026 - The US ad-free tier becomes Prime Video Ultra at $4.99 a month
- May 11, 2026 - Amazon's Upfront sets November 11 for season three; the release cites over 185 million viewers and ranks season two among the top five returning seasons by viewers
- July 9, 2026 - Prime Video announces its San Diego Comic-Con program, with a shared Hall H slot for Blade Runner 2099 and The Rings of Power
- July 2026, earlier in Comic-Con week - Jamie Campbell Bower revealed as Celeborn and Zubin Varla as Khamûl the Easterling
- July 24, 2026 - Hall H panel before over 6,500 fans: teaser trailer, three character reveals, Simon Pegg as the voice of the Balrog
- July 30, 2026 - Amazon reports Q2 advertising revenue up 26% to $19.8 billion
- October 21, 2026 - Official trailer and the three-batch release schedule
- October 29, 2026 - Amazon reports Q3 advertising revenue up 11% to $19.64 billion
- November 11, 2026 - First four episodes of season three
- November 18, 2026 - Episodes 305 and 306
- November 25, 2026 - Final two episodes

Summary
Who: Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios, with Peter Friedlander, head of global television; showrunners J.D. Payne and Patrick McKay; and cast members including Eddie Marsan, Andrew Richardson, Adam Young, Jamie Campbell Bower, Zubin Varla and Simon Pegg.
What: Between June 2025 and October 2026, Amazon's releases for The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power raised the series' claimed audience from over 170 million to over 185 million viewers and changed the season two ranking from first by hours watched to top five by viewers within a 91-day window, without publishing a method. The releases also set out the Upfront date announcement, the Comic-Con character reveals and the start of filming at Shepperton Studios.
When: The releases are dated June 12, 2025, May 11, 2026, July 9, 2026, July 24, 2026 and October 21, 2026. Season three premieres on November 11, 2026, with further episodes on November 18 and 25.
Where: New York for the Upfront, Hall H at San Diego Comic-Con for the July panel, Shepperton Studios in the UK for production, and Prime Video for the release, in a catalog Amazon says reaches more than 240 countries and territories.
Why: Amazon describes the series as one of its strongest drivers of new Prime sign-ups, and in the US a new Prime member sees ads by default. The audience claims are the main public evidence for that case, yet the measure behind them has changed and none of the figures is explained.
